Diagnosis: The failure is caused by the previous point_toward term using controlled_entity="gripped_object". The runtime error explicitly says point_toward only supports robot_frame as controlled_entity, so the upright-orientation constraint must be represented without point_toward on the gripped object. The smallest repair is to replace that point_toward term with an axis_align term for can_center_frame local -y codirectional with world +z, while keeping the grasp and fixed-position constraints unchanged.
Reasoning: This remains one conjunctive controller stage. object_grasped with the gripper_closed condition keeps the can held in the closed panda_fingertip gripper; individual finger joint coordinates and finger squeeze effort are not directly representable beyond this grasp/closed metadata. freeze_position keeps the can_center_frame origin fixed at its start-of-stage world position within 0.01 m and is the only position operator in the stage. axis_align makes the gripped can_center_frame local -y axis codirectional with world +z, which makes the cylindrical can upright while leaving rotation about that same long axis unconstrained. The start-of-stage panda_fingertip-to-can_center_frame transform preservation and continuous monitoring requirements are not directly representable as separate TermAPI constraints, but object_grasped captures the required coupled grasp during manipulation.
